measured: bash examples/steer/test.sh prints 'passed 96, failed 0'; every check asserts on a value read back out of a run report, a ledger record, a decision journal, a log line or an exit status, and the gate has a floor under the count as well as a zero-failure condition, so a gutted copy that counts nothing exits 1

all four entry documents validate against examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json, and all four payload.steer declarations against examples/steer/schemas/steer.schema.json, using the reference example's one validator
the four doors carry four actors, four run ids and four correlation ids through one unit declaration, and the effect decision at every door is identical in point, action, effect, rule and resource

no rule of either bundle reads context.entry_kind: the door is an attribute of the input and not a branch in the rules, asserted over every condition path of both bundles including the field-comparison operands

correlation.depth is declared by the caller and consumed by nothing: the external door run with depth 99 and with the member deleted returns the same status, the same nine decisions in point, action, effect, rule and resource, the same stream and the same refusals, while every record of both carries the depth derived from the delegation chain, which is 3 and which neither run declared

the task specification is the one intent.workflow_ref names and not a default: an envelope pointing at a unit declaring a free attempt class puts f-grunt on the model-call decision where the shipped declaration puts i-fast, and the run costs 0 micros instead of the routing table's price, with no --unit flag given
every decision of every door precedes the first metered call of the action it admits (decisions_taken equals decided_before_that_action_spent, per door), and a denied dispatch spent nothing
every decision carries a rule id, a bundle digest and an input digest - allow as well as deny - asserted over every row of every door

an allow is spent when its action fires or is abandoned: the effect is decided twice on one run, and a rule set activated while the unit is parked flips the second decision from allow to deny under a different policy version, so the effect never fires and the unit ends failed
the pre-pause decision still replays to allow against the bundle version it was pinned to, after a different bundle has started serving

deliberate breakage: carrying the pre-pause allow across the resume instead of deciding again takes the dispatch.tool_call decision rows from two to one - counted out of the decision rows themselves, not read off the runner's own decisions_at_effect field - and an effect the rules in force now refuse is applied, with the ledger recording decided_again false
bundle v2 is bundle v1 plus exactly one rule at one index, with an identical entity model and an identical deny-by-default, asserted structurally rather than trusted between two hand-kept files
approve continues with the proposed artifact and edit continues with the reviewer's body, which is a different document; both reach the disposition accept

the declared surface changes what a decision may carry and not what the platform stores: the same 400-byte edit body is refused 422 by a surface declaring max_edit_bytes 256 and applied by one declaring 65536, from one store, and the stream renders more of the same event log than the parked item does
steering.retries_permitted is read at the loop bound: 1 gives exactly one retry record and two attempts, 0 gives none and one
steering.escalation.steps_permitted is read after the attempts are spent: 1 gives exactly one escalation record and never two, 0 gives an escalation-declined record and no escalated ask

the escalated ask is parked for, and decided by, the authority the unit names, on the trigger the unit states; a decider who is not that authority is denied by deny-decision-outside-named-authority with the work never run
steering.decisions_offered is read: a unit that does not offer edit refuses the edit at 422 on the same door that accepted it

one decision is applied once: a redelivery returns duplicate, a second different decision on a decided ask is 409 and becomes a human.refused event, and the same envelope submitted twice parks no second ask
the decision returns on the run's own correlation id and adds the deciding actor to the delegation chain

decision_delay_seconds is read against gate.deadline_seconds on both sides: past the deadline the ask is terminal, ask.expired is emitted, the late decision is 504, the effect never fires and the unit ends failed rather than waiting; short of it the sweep the store refuses comes back as a typed 422 with the ask still open, no ask.expired event and no traceback
all eight published event types are produced across the four doors, and every type emitted is one the human-interaction capability publishes

the task lifecycle on the ledger is submitted, input-required, working, completed (or failed), every name from the published set, and the runner refuses a state outside it; every disposition is one of the ontology's four

reconnect keeps the unit id and negotiates what the class offers; restart returns a new unit whose state digest equals the pre-turn checkpoint's, unchanged before any further call; replace returns a new unit whose state digest equals the stuck unit's own and not the checkpoint's

intervention_policy.checkpoint_before_turn is read: with the pre-turn checkpoint a restart returns the unit to the state before the turn, without it the restart's own checkpoint is the state after it, and the two restarts return different state digests

stall_first_turn is read: the first turn runs past the unit's wall ceiling and the boundary ends it terminated by the budget ceiling with more frames than a healthy turn, while the retry's turn ends end_turn
reconnect succeeded against a unit the boundary had already destroyed, and the report says so rather than hiding it
intervention_policy.permitted is read before the decision point: an operation the unit does not permit is refused 422 and produces no steer.intervention decision at all

the mandates the rules read are derived from the envelope's delegation chain: the same replace verb is denied for a chain with no delegated hop and allowed for one with, with the work never run on the deny
a containment class that offers no pause, resume or fork answers the checkpoint and the operator's verb with a typed 501 rather than emulating them, and the pair differs on four execution-model axes
the 501 has no row in the shared closed problem registry, and is reported as absent rather than re-typed

fail closed at five enforcement points: with the engine made unreachable at admission.entry, steer.intervention, dispatch.model_call, dispatch.tool_call and steer.decision in turn, every one refuses, the work never ran, that action spent nothing, no allow follows, and the record says undecided with no rule to attribute it to - distinct from a policy deny

registration is what makes a point decidable: one request at a sixth point, dispatch.data_query, is allowed by its own rule with the work run when the point is registered and refused decision-point-unregistered 422 with nothing run, nothing spent and no journal row when it is not; and the same point's rule reads a path outside the typed engine's entity model, so that engine declares the point a conformance subset and refuses adapter-unavailable rather than answering allow
a cross-tenant unit is refused 403 at admission with the rule named, no cell is admitted and nothing is spent
a subject the platform holds no tenancy for is refused 401 before any decision is asked for
a malformed envelope exits 2 with a 422 naming the missing field and writes no ledger

a caller that adds a policy_version member to its steer declaration is refused 422 with the member named, and a caller that adds an advisory field to the decision request is refused 422 with the closed vocabulary quoted
the ceiling remaining is computed by the platform and read by a rule: a ceiling that no longer covers the effect denies it by name where the full ceiling allows it
effect.scope is read together with the chain's mandates: an external-scope effect is denied without a mandate and allowed with one
the closed problem registry keeps rule_id on a policy denial and drops decision_point, input_digest, policy_version and spend_delta_micros, measured by name

the swap is configuration: all four doors run on a second decision engine and return identical decisions - point, action, effect and rule id over twenty-four decisions, and an identical input digest for each of the twenty-one whose input was the same bytes - while the two engines differ on all four declared execution-model axes

no product, engine or policy-language name appears in any source file of this directory, in any artefact a run of it writes, or in the README outside the standards and adapters tables, and no entry document names an adapter, an engine or a policy version

the ledger chain verifies, a one-character edit is detected, and every record of the longest run carries the run id, correlation id, actor, delegation depth, entry kind and idempotency key across the thirteen record kinds that run writes; the README's receipt row names exactly the nineteen kinds the whole visible check writes, checked in both directions against the ledgers
provenance.cites equals exactly the set of ids the example's files carry, checked in both directions, and FLOOR equals visible_checks_counted
docs/architecture/proposed/steer.json carries seven proposed blueprint gaps, every one with a research query and none with an invented mechanism
produced by 75-steer-author on 2026-09-04; the example-provenance shape has no member for the producing identity, so it is recorded here, which is the same misplacement the run area recorded as a gap
claimed: that swapping the decision language is a configuration change for two live engines: both adapters measured here evaluate in process, so the swap is proved across two execution models and claimed across two products (README gap 9)
that the standards named hold at the versions given; no specification page was fetched (STATUS row 14)

that the request and response shape used here is the published decision API's: subject, action, resource, context and an effect with its deciding rule are this repository's reading of that shape from a search-sourced description, and no specification was fetched to validate a request against

that the rule set is a rule set anyone would ship: it is a fixture of eleven rules over five decision points, and the corpus the two engines agree on is the twenty-four decisions four doors of one unit produce (README gap 8)

that a person decided anything: every decision here is scripted from the entry document, so the human boundary is measured for its authority, replay, deadline and refusal behaviour and not for what a reviewer would do
that the decision point is affordable at the rate this example implies - one decision per action per unit - since nothing here measures either half of the decision's latency (README gap 9)
that a bundle is immutable and signed: it is versioned by the digest of its canonical bytes and immutable on disk, and nothing signs or verifies it (README gap 4)
that a decision is replayable months later: it is replayable within the process that took it, because the journal the replay reads is an attribute on the engine object (README gap 6)

that the operator's verbs act on a live unit: the boundary has already destroyed the stuck unit by the time they run, and no operation on the isolation interface reports whether a unit may still be driven (README gap 3)
that the hidden deciding check for this example exists: the index looks for one outside examples/, which this author's brief did not permit writing (README gap 10)
